content.title: About
content.content: Pita is a flat bread made from wheat flour, typical of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines. The dough is rolled into round discs and baked at high temperature, causing a pocket to form in the centre as steam expands.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pita can be soft or slightly crisp depending on baking time.
Traditionally it is served with hummus, kebab, falafel and other Middle Eastern dishes.
Bread shapes similar to modern pita are mentioned in ancient Egyptian texts.
The pocket inside pita is created by rapid evaporation of moisture from the dough during baking.
In some regions pita is called “Arabic bread” or “lavash”.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pita provides a quick source of energy thanks to its high content of complex carbohydrates.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other breads, traditional pita contains little fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour used for pita is rich in thiamine, niacin and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: Pita provides iron, magnesium and phosphorus, supporting blood health and bone function.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Its soft texture and small size make pita easy to eat quickly and digest.

items.title: Gluten intolerance
items.content: Pita contains gluten, so people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid it.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because its carbohydrates are absorbed quickly, pita should be eaten in moderation, especially by people with diabetes.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some commercially prepared pitas contain added salt; those with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut pita along the side to open a “pocket” and fill it with meat, vegetables, sauces or salads. It can also be used as a sandwich base, served alongside soups, or as a side for grilled dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pita in an airtight bag at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, place it in a paper bag in the refrigerator to retain softness without becoming soggy. Freeze in a plastic bag for up to 3 months; reheat in the oven or microwave before use.
